summary: Follow-on: Orphic Hymns appended editorial prose not dropped (chunks 087-090 'Hymn LXXV Muse' + 103 'Hymn LXXXVI Death' are pure Taylor commentary, mislabeled as hymns)

analysis.author: corpus-quality
analysis.content:
PR #83 REVIEW FINDING #1 (2026-08-20): The PR's headline claim — removing retrievable pollution where queries about Orphic theology surfaced Taylor's essay instead of hymns — is only PARTIALLY MET.

drop_before_marker stripped the LEADING front matter (pages 1-6, chunks old 001-034), but the SAME dissertation-style commentary is appended to note-heavy hymn pages:
- Source page hoo80.htm (Hymn LXXV 'THE MUSES') has the hymn text + Taylor's essay on the Muses
- Source page hoo91.htm (Hymn LXXXVI 'DEATH') has the hymn text + Taylor's philosophical commentary on commerce/philosophy

When these pages exceed max_tokens=800, the chunker sub-splits them into (part N) chunks that inherit the hymn label. Verified content of the mislabeled chunks:
- .087 (DB .053) 'Hymn LXXV. THE MUSES (part 2)' — 793 tokens of Taylor's essay on Plato's Phædrus, poetic fury, Muses as divine motion. Pure prose, no hymn text.
- .088 (DB .054) through .090 likely same pattern
- .103 (DB .069) 'Hymn LXXXVI. DEATH (part 2)' — 429 tokens of Taylor's essay on Thames commerce, the Dæmon of commerce, philosophical retreats. Pure prose, no hymn text.

These chunks carry the hymn's label but their body is editorial commentary. A query for 'the Muses' returns ~3000 tokens of Taylor's essay labeled 'Hymn LXXV. THE MUSES' — the exact defect the PR claims to fix.

analysis.author: corpus-quality
analysis.content:
VERIFIED ON PR #83 BRANCH + DB: The editorial prose chunks still carry verified tags and live edges — the exact 'retrievable pollution' the PR claims to fix is still present:

DB state for chunks 087-090 + 103 (all labeled as Hymn LXXV/LXXXVI 'parts'):
- 087 'Hymn LXXV. THE MUSES (part 2)': 5 accepted tags, 22 edges
- 088 'Hymn LXXV. THE MUSES (part 3)': 16 accepted tags, 30 edges
- 089 'Hymn LXXV. THE MUSES (part 4)': 2 accepted tags, 21 edges
- 090 'Hymn LXXV. THE MUSES (part 5)': 2 accepted tags, 8 edges
- 103 'Hymn LXXXVI. DEATH (part 2)': 15 accepted tags, 32 edges
TOTAL: 40 accepted tags + 113 live edges on pure editorial prose

PR #83 did NOT fix this. drop_before_marker only strips the leading contiguous front-matter block. The appended editorial commentary on note-heavy pages (hoo80 = Hymn LXXV + 1500+ words of Taylor's essay on the Muses; hoo63 = Hymn LVIII + Gesner commentary) was chunked into (part N) sub-chunks that inherited the hymn labels. These chunks are retrievable pollution: a query for 'Muses' or 'Orphic theology' surfaces Taylor's essay, not the hymn.

analysis.author: corpus-quality
analysis.content:
FIX OPTIONS:

(A) Pipeline code change (guru-dev/Driver) — the proper fix:
   - In scripts/chunk.py, after page-as-chunk splits a note-heavy page into (part N) chunks, apply a 'no_hymn_pattern' check: if a chunk's body doesn't start with the hymn invocation pattern (Roman numeral + 'TO' or period), flag it as apparatus via staged_cleanups.
   - OR: add a post-split 'appended editorial' stripper that removes Taylor's essay commentary from hymn page tails before chunking (a companion to drop_before_marker for the tail, call it drop_after_marker or tail_strip_patterns).
   - This is NOT a config-only fix — it requires chunk.py changes to handle the split sub-chunks.

(B) Config-only workaround (limited): Add 'FOOTNOTES' to a tail-strip pattern — but this would also strip legitimate footnotes from hymn text, and the review explicitly flagged this risk.

The 40 accepted tags + 113 edges on these 5 chunks need to be: (1) deleted (they're curation on editorial prose), and (2) the chunks themselves need to be either dropped or re-stripped. The tag deletion is corpus-quality's orphan cleanup; the chunk re-stripping is a re-chunk (Driver).
